subject: Pilot billing: overage protection & context-slicing behavior
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Confusing pilot invoices — short sessions being charged extra

Hi Hannah,

Quick note from our engineering and procurement teams after our first week of the pilot. We're seeing a couple of surprising line items on the usage report: short, single-turn inference calls are being billed at the same minimum as ~10-turn sessions. In particular: when our UI spins up ephemeral sessions for previewing a 1-2 sentence summary, the reported "session length" looks inflated and we get charged toward the per-session minimum.

We tried to follow the docs on context-slicing and KV cache TTL but the behavior doesn't match expectations. Can you explain:

- How the billing window treats very short sessions (< 5 tokens generated) vs longer multi-turn dialogs?
- Is the KV/prefix cache shared across user previews in a way that counts toward a single session?
- Do you offer any overage protection / pilot credits to avoid surprise early charges while we validate UX patterns?

We're running this pilot across a subset of users and want to avoid an invoice spike that forces us to pause. Appreciate a quick rundown and any temporary concessions you can offer while we tune requests.

Thanks,
Alice
Procurement Lead — Acme Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confusing pilot invoices — short sessions being charged extra

Hi Alice — thanks for flagging and sorry for the surprise. High level answers up front, then I will loop in Marcus for the exact invoice/credit mechanics and Monica for the runtime/kv-cache details.

Short answers:
- Billing windows: we meter at the request level but also apply a per-call minimum when calls are below the configured quantum for that account. That quantum was set to a 256-token floor for your trial tenant to simplify pilot pricing.
- KV/prefix cache: by default the cache is per-model + per-tenant; short previews can reattach to an active context and appear as a continuation if the client reuses the same session id.
- Pilot protection: we can issue a one-time courtesy credit for unexpected pilot overages and temporarily lower the session minimum for your trial tenant while you iterate.

Ask from us: can you send a couple of example request IDs or timestamps (UTC) where you see the inflated charge? Monica — can you confirm whether the Acme tenant is currently on the 256-token floor and whether prefix reuse is likely causing the counts? Marcus — what credit do we want to propose for a pilot; I suggest we model a capped credit equivalent to 25% of October pilot spend or up to $2k, whichever is lower, as a quick safety net.

Alice — happy to set up a 30-minute sync if that helps.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-23T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confusing pilot invoices — short sessions being charged extra

Hi Alice, Hannah — I pulled the usage and invoice lines for your tenant and summarized the behavior. Attaching a short calculation CSV that walks through the October samples.

Summary of findings:
- Your tenant is on a trial quantum setting that enforces a per-request minimum equivalent to 256 tokens for generation metering; that minimum was applied at tenant provisioning.
- Several preview flows open ephemeral sessions but then reuse the UI session id. When that happens the platform treats the preview as a continuation (KV cache attach) and bills under the same session aggregation logic — this can push a small preview into the min bucket if there's prior context attached.
- We see ~18 requests on Oct 14 and Oct 19 that are under 12 generated tokens but got lifted to the 256-token floor due to session aggregation.

Proposed commercial fixes (quick):
1) Immediate: apply a one-time pilot credit of $1,800 against the October invoice to cover the identified mischarges (covers ~90% of the flagged lines).
2) Short-term configuration: temporarily drop your tenant quantum from 256 to 32 tokens for the remainder of the pilot (no contract change); this prevents short previews from hitting the 256 floor.
3) Medium-term: we can enable an "ephemeral" session tag for your preview endpoints (non-billing-aggregated). That would require a minor runtime flag change — Monica, can you note the engineering effort and expected timeline?

If that plan sounds ok to Acme we will: apply the $1.8k credit, change the tenant quantum to 32, and schedule the ephemeral-tag work as a low-priority item for next sprint.

Comments welcome — Hannah, happy to defer to you on the credit amount if you'd like to be more generous.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot-credit-calculation.csv (rows: sample_request_id, timestamp, generated_tokens, billed_tokens, adjustment_amount)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confusing pilot invoices — short sessions being charged extra

Thanks all — quick technical confirmation and implementation notes.

What happened: the client SDK reuses session IDs for UI-level previews. Our runtime links that session id to the tenant's context bucket. If a user opens the preview while the bucket still has prior prompt tokens (KV entries), the runtime merges the preview as a continuation and the metering pipeline reports the total effective context length. The metering pipeline then applies the tenant quantum floor.

Options and effort estimate:
- Temporary config change (low effort): set tenant quantum from 256 -> 32. Live in minutes after config push. No code changes.
- Ephemeral session tag (medium effort): add a session flag that prevents aggregation into billing buckets and forces per-call metering. Approx 2 engineers for 3-4 days; we can ship as a feature toggle in the next sprint. Requires minor SDK opt-in.
- Long-term instrumentation (low-medium): emit a lightweight telemetry marker on preview requests so billing reports can separate preview vs canonical flows for reporting/discounting. 1-2 weeks.

Recommendation: do the tenant quantum change immediately + grant the one-time $1,800 credit so Acme can keep the pilot running. Then schedule ephemeral-tag work as a sprint item. I've attached a small sample of session traces (session-samples.jsonl) that show the request ids you mentioned.

Alice — if you want I can also join a short call to review traces and confirm the tenant change doesn't affect your production routes.

Monica Patel
Product Manager, Runtime — Redwood Inference
Attachment: session-samples.jsonl (ndjson; fields: request_id, session_id, model, generated_tokens, kv_hits)
